findings.location: Scene 3, B6 and B7, Jaina's explanation and her question to Havel
findings.passage: "It isn't mixed into the grain," Jaina said. "It's put on it." || "Not the sacks. Corin's already put those on the south road, and I've read enough of them tonight to know they'll tell you nothing about who filled them." She didn't look at Corin. "The crock, Captain."
findings.problem: Jaina's voice sheet has an explicit red flag: 'Do not build her lines as "not X, Y" corrections. Say the true thing first.' Both of her most important S3 lines open with the negation and then correct it. This is the only remaining voice-sheet violation in her dialogue, and it lands on the mechanism reveal (B6) and on the line that sides her with the plan that holds (B7).
findings.fix: Lead with the true thing. B6: "It's put on the grain. A coat, too thin to see..." (drop 'It isn't mixed into the grain' completely; 'put on' already says it). B7: open on the crock: "The crock, Captain. Where is it by the time your clerk gets there?" Then the sacks can follow as her reason: "Corin's already put the sacks on the south road, and I've read enough of them tonight to know they won't tell you who filled them." Keep 'She didn't look at Corin.'

findings.location: Scene 1, B2, line beginning 'Jaina hadn't said a word since she sat down'
findings.passage: Jaina hadn't said a word since she sat down. She had been sitting with the staff between her boots and her eyes half shut...
findings.problem: This contradicts the page. Jaina sits ('Jaina sat, setting the heel of the staff...') and then speaks twice: she introduces herself and the tally-man referral, and she answers Corin ('No. Nobody sent me.'). The B3 interior also leans on her silence ('Jaina had sat through all of his talk at the table without a word'). That later line is accurate, because she said nothing during Havel's briefing. The first one is not.
findings.fix: Anchor the silence to Havel's talk, not to her sitting down: 'Jaina hadn't said a word since she told Corin nobody had sent her', or 'Jaina had not spoken through any of Havel's talk.'

findings.location: Scenes 2-3: Hurdle Lane walk, Fenner's yard, the dead drop, the chalk paragraph
findings.passage: talking the whole way, the way a man talks about a house he has lived in all his life. || He was simply looking at the yard the way a man on a wall looks at a road. || he put his left hand flat on the stone as if to steady himself, the way a tired man does. || A man who owned a lane drew it like that, over and over, the way a farmer walks the bounds of his own field.
findings.problem: Four ', the way a man...' similes. They are one comparison frame used over and over, and the mannered checker caps it at 2 (M13 over cap). The dead-drop one doubles 'as if to steady himself' with 'the way a tired man does', so it says the same thing twice.
findings.fix: Keep the two that carry Sylvanas's idiom: the hoist man 'the way a man on a wall looks at a road' (ground-reading) and the farmer walking his bounds (her argument about Havel). Cut 'the way a tired man does' from the dead drop, since 'as if to steady himself' already does the work. Recast Havel's walk-talk plainly, e.g. 'talking the whole way about the yards as if he had built them.'

findings.passage: The other man was already moving. || Jaina was already getting the staff under her and her feet under the staff || Jaina was already turning on the staff. || Corin was already buckling the satchel.
findings.problem: '[Character] was already [verb]ing' is the chapter's one shorthand for anticipation. It appears four times, twice for Jaina and twice for Corin. Each one alone is fine. Together they make the same beat, and the B3 instance especially takes the sting out of the B8 moment where Jaina coming round the table before Sylvanas asks is supposed to matter.
findings.fix: Keep Corin's at the close ('Corin was already buckling the satchel'), where it shows him moving toward the danger. Replace the others with plain action. For example, S1: 'The other man had the stool out before Havel finished'. B3: 'Jaina had the staff under her and her feet under the staff'. B3 later: 'Jaina turned on the staff.' Save Jaina's anticipation for B8.

findings.location: Scene 3 opening at the post, and the chalk
findings.passage: The night came in through the gap in the shutter, warm, and sweet with grain. / ...A moth came in through the gap in the shutter and landed on the paper || Havel answered at once, getting up and going to the canvas on the wall. (S1) / He picked it up, going to the canvas on the wall. (S3)
findings.problem: Two adjacent sentences both use 'came in through the gap in the shutter'. 'Going to the canvas on the wall' repeats across scenes. In S3 the participle is also a timing glitch: he picks up the chalk and then crosses the room, but 'picked it up, going to' makes the two actions simultaneous. These read like participials added to hit the texture target. Texture is now 99.5, so there is room to undo them.
findings.fix: Vary the moth: 'A moth found the same gap and landed on the paper.' Make the chalk two actions: 'He picked it up and went to the canvas.' The compound rate can absorb it.

findings.passage: Eight strokes, put where the eight had stood. A cross on the wall at the mouth of the first loading lane. ... She touched the single stroke she'd put halfway up the lane. || Jaina looked at the ring she'd drawn for the crock
findings.problem: The drawing paragraph lists a cross for the drop crack and no stroke for the runner, so 'the single stroke she'd put halfway up the lane' points at a mark the reader never saw drawn. Also, in 'Jaina looked at the ring she'd drawn', the 'she' grammatically refers to Jaina. Sylvanas drew it. The plan says the marks lying side by side carry the fit, so the marks need to be exact.
findings.fix: Add the runner stroke when she draws ('One stroke up the lane from it, alone.'), or have her touch the cross instead. Change 'the ring she'd drawn for the crock' to 'the ring Sylvanas had drawn for the crock', or to 'the ring for the crock'.

findings.passage: The ostler had watched four tall Thalassian animals come in through his gate sweating and walling their eyes, taking her silver without a word about any of it.
findings.problem: The trailing participle follows 'sweating and walling their eyes', which belongs to the horses, so 'taking her silver' reads first as something the horses did. This is a misattached participle in the chapter's second paragraph.
findings.fix: Make the ostler the subject of the payment: 'The ostler had watched four tall Thalassian animals come in through his gate sweating and walling their eyes, and had taken her silver without a word about any of it.' Or split it: '...walling their eyes. He took her silver without a word about any of it.'

findings.location: Scene 2 B4 and Scene 3 B7, the Havel tally
findings.passage: That was the second time he had pointed her somewhere other than where she was looking—once at the post, now here. || He'd pointed past Tenter Row on the way down, too. She didn't say so. || There it went: Hurdle Lane, for the third time tonight
findings.problem: Advisory only. The plan wants the Havel plant 'low-key, findable on a second read'. Sylvanas keeps an explicit running count ('second time', 'too', 'third time'), so a first-time reader is handed the pattern. Each instance carries its fair counter-reading ('So would other men', the unfairness admission), so this is not a POV or plan violation. Together, though, they push the plant toward underlined.
findings.fix: Drop the count from B4 and keep only the observation: 'A man who knew his own streets and wanted a stranger on the ones he trusted would point like that. So would other men.' The Tenter Row recall in S3 and the 'third time' chalk paragraph are then the only explicit tallies, which is enough.

findings.location: Scene 3, B8, Cyndia's rope-walk report vs. Scene 2 description
findings.passage: a hasp and a padlock on each door (S2) / The captain's men watched them in, and the lock went on from inside. (S3)
findings.problem: A hasp and padlock is an outside lock. 'The lock went on from inside' either contradicts that or adds a bar or inner bolt that S2 never showed. It is minor, but Cyndia reports in exact event order and Ch8 may stage action at these doors.
findings.fix: Make Cyndia's line 'and they barred it from inside', or give the S2 shed doors an inner bar as well as the outside padlock. Flag it to the continuity gate either way.

summary: The revision fixed all twelve findings from round 0. Texture went from 68.8 to 99.5 and no dimension is off target. Necromancy is named with Jaina's hitch, the rooftop re-narration is gone, the B8 sentence-finishing device is broken, and Havel's 'we' and fair-play steering are in place. Emotional life is strong in every scene: the clerk's nib, 'Half the ground in this town was ink', the trust-versus-results argument, the crack she leaves alone, the window stare, and the unfair-to-slow-men chalk paragraph. There are at least four registers (dry humour, warmth at the edges, dread, exhaustion), POV is clean, and all eight beats are dramatized. What remains is line-level: Jaina's two 'not X, Y' openings (a voice-sheet red flag, medium), a factual slip ('hadn't said a word since she sat down'), the 'the way a man' simile overused, the 'already' readiness beat repeated, and a few small mark and lock inconsistencies. These go to the downstream passes, and none of them blocks a pass.
